where_the_residual_comes_from.fork_vs_sealed_module_run_fresh_here: BITWISE IDENTICAL. Tolerance 0.0, worst difference 0.0 over the same 8,320 scientific leaves, 0 digest mismatches, 0 discrete mismatches. The fork adds nothing.

where_the_residual_comes_from.reading: The 3.44e-15 and the 3,072 differing sha256 digests of floating-point arrays are the difference between this platform and R6l's producing platform, not a property of the fork. A last-bit difference in an array changes its digest completely, which is exactly the case R6k-W1's comparator counts rather than fails. Without the fresh sealed run those 3,072 would have been unattributable.

non_vacuity.perturbation_control: R6k-W1's C1 applied here: one scientific leaf moved by 1e-9 returns NOT_EQUIVALENT. The comparison is not one that agrees with everything.
non_vacuity.leaf_accounting: 19,200 shared leaves: 8,320 scientific compared under tolerance, 5,120 discrete compared exactly, 5,760 identity (digest) leaves counted. Every non-digest leaf was compared. R6k-W1's scientific-fraction floor is that round's rule and is not imported here.

post_freeze_controls.C_wiring: PASS. With the sealed depths injected in a PERMUTED order, build_map_tasks computes them in that order, so the grid reaches the numerics and not only the labels. A companion test rebinds DEPTH_COORDS alone -- the fork the execution blocker described -- and the numerics keep the sealed order: the check fails on the fork it exists to reject. The preregistered equivalence test cannot make this distinction at all, because at the sealed grid a labels-only fork and a correct one produce identical rows.
post_freeze_controls.C_no_mutation: PASS. The imported sealed modules keep DEPTHS and DEPTH_COORDS by value and by identity, and keep their own sys.modules entries.
post_freeze_controls.status: These inform the reading of the verdict and cannot change it.

what_the_round_found_that_it_was_not_ask.the_blocker_was_incomplete: The execution blocker named DEPTH_COORDS as the obstacle to parameterising R6l. It is one of three depth bindings: DEPTHS in equal_resource_reservoir is what the numerics iterate, and a literal store count of 320 assumes five depths. A fork built to the blocker's description would have passed this round's preregistered test and then crashed at the first held-out depth -- the sealed validators fail closed, so it would have failed loudly rather than silently, but Part B would not have run.
what_the_round_found_that_it_was_not_ask.the_kill_condition_is_now_executable: build_fork refuses held-out depths without a licence artifact whose verdict is EQUIVALENT_ON_SEALED_GRID. The first version matched the decimal spelling, so '0.2' passed where '0.20' was refused; it now keys on the binary64 value. Fixed before any commit.
what_the_round_found_that_it_was_not_ask.the_tolerance_clause_named_nothing: 'path-specific tolerances' do not exist; the comparator takes one scalar. Run at R6k-W1's 1e-10, introducing nothing.

evidence_ceiling_unchanged: A pass licenses the fork as a stand-in ONLY on R6l's five measured depths. It does not establish equivalence at held-out depths -- where the sealed implementation is undefined, so there is nothing to be equivalent TO -- and does not itself support any Part B, architecture, hardware, advantage or cognition claim.
what_is_not_claimed: not equivalence at any held-out depth; none was evaluated and equality at five points cannot prove equality at five others
not that Part B is licensed to conclude anything; only that its receiver can now be constructed by a code path shown bitwise identical to the sealed one where both are defined
not independent witnessing: producer and verifier are the same development line
not cross-platform reproduction: one platform, no CI job
typed_remainders: [R]_extrapolation: equality on five reference depths cannot prove equality where the sealed implementation is undefined.
[R]_shared_lineage: producer and verifier remain the same development line.

[R]_implementation: delegation by verified re-execution avoids duplication and leaves the sealed modules untouched, but executes the same bytes twice in two namespaces; exactly one import-time depth binding exists (truncation_cost_report's default argument) and is off R6l's path, asserted by a static call graph that would miss a function passed as a value.
[R]_grid_length: the fork runs five-depth grids only, because the sealed store count is a literal.
